result:
The app asks `/auth/me` once, when it loads, and keeps the answer in React Query. `src/app/provider.tsx` wraps the app in `AuthLoader` from `src/lib/auth.tsx`, which calls `getUser` (`GET /auth/me`) before rendering and shows a spinner meanwhile. `src/lib/auth.tsx` builds the auth hooks with `configureAuth` from `react-query-auth`, so `useUser()` returns the cached user anywhere in the app. Routes under `/app` are wrapped in `ProtectedRoute` in `src/app/router.tsx`. If `user.data` is empty, it renders a `Navigate` to `paths.auth.login.getHref(location.pathname)`. Signing in and out updates the same cached user through `useLogin` and `useLogout`.

Every request goes through the shared Axios instance in `src/lib/api-client.ts`. Its response interceptor shows an error toast with the server's message for any failure. If the status is 401, it sets `window.location.href` to the login path, passing `redirectTo`. That redirect is a full page load, not a React Router navigation.

The 401 handling has a bug. It reads `redirectTo` from `new URLSearchParams()`, which is always empty, so it falls back to `window.location.pathname`. The current query string is dropped, and any `redirectTo` already in the URL is ignored. Since the interceptor also runs for the `/auth/me` call on load, a signed-out visitor is probably sent to sign-in from any page, including `/`. I did not run the app to confirm that. I made no file changes.

Files involved: `src/app/provider.tsx`, `src/lib/auth.tsx`, `src/lib/api-client.ts`, `src/app/router.tsx`, `src/config/paths.ts`, `src/components/layouts/auth-layout.tsx`.
